A minimum of two years construction experience with hands-on experience in multiple construction related trades including carpentry (framing, roofing, drywall, etc.), plumbing (e.g, water and propane lines), electrical, welding, masonry, and basic vehicle maintenance and repair; and knowledge and understanding of California building codes, as well as hazardous materials and general safety policies.
Demonstrated experience supervising employees and volunteers
Drive vehicles, tractors, trailers and other transport systems as needed
Basic understanding and experience in trail and barbed wire and fence construction and maintenance.

Facilities and Grounds Management: Repair and maintenance of facilities and grounds, including painting, carpentry, electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling systems (air conditioners, propane heaters and stoves, refrigeration units), water systems (waterlines and trenches, well pumps, storage tanks, filters and general plumbing), backup power generators, roads and berms, gates and fences, trails and signs. Maintain, repair, and drive vehicles, tractors, trailers and other transport systems as needed. Organize and maintain tools, supplies and maintenance facilities (e.g., shops, sheds, yards). Custodial duties include: sweeping, mopping, cleaning sinks and toilets, washing windows and screens, dusting furniture, and trash and recycling removal. Inspect and maintain fire safety systems and equipment and supplies. Maintain a safe, visually aesthetic and functional landscape around facilities that incorporates native plant horticulture and schemes that preserve the environmental and cultural/historical integrity of the reserve. Work with, part-time employees and supervise volunteers, which may include supervising these positions (60% time)

User Management and General Administration: Responsible for reserve operations when other reserve staff are off-site or on extended absences, including operation of main office and communications. Assist the Resident Director and other staff as needed with visitor use of facilities for research, teaching and outreach activities. Assist with user arrival/departure, including preparing lodging, use of laboratory and classroom, communicating Deep Canyon rules and regulations, check-out inspections, and billing or fee collection. Support researchers and classes with equipment and utility needs. Coordinate reserve use to avoid impacts and conflicts among other users. Select and purchase supplies and equipment following UCR Purchasing policies. Perform accounting tasks as needed and maintain all files and records. Assist with management of user applications and reservations including RAMS documentation and sign-in sheets, billing invoices, and correspondence as needed. Under the direction of the Reserve Director, assist in organizing workshops, meetings, and conferences; participate in public outreach activities including teaching, guided tours, and lectures/demonstrations. (20% time)

Construction: As directed and supervised by the Resident Director, participate in or lead the design and construction of small projects involving facilities repairs, renovations and upgrades, campground facilities, storage facilities, decking, walkways, bird feeders or other research and educational props. Assist other reserve and UCR staff with planning, design and implementation of major facilities additions and upgrades. Supervise and work with vendors and construction contractors as needed. (15% time)

Resource Management: Provide skilled labor and applied techniques in support on-going management or research projects, including erosion control, native vegetation restoration and protection, rare species habitat management and protection of archaeological sites. Perform regular patrols to maintain reserve boundaries and redirect public trespass. Assist in recording and maintaining on-site climate and other data monitoring systems. (5% time)
Required to hold valid driver's license, have a driving record that is in accordance with local policies/procedures, and/or enroll in the California Employer Pull Notice Program.
California State contractor's license

Experience with maintenance of a variety of vehicles and engines, including tractors, 4WD trucks, passenger vehicles, small motors (generators, power tools, etc.
Ability to read and interpret building plans, and to implement new construction based on plans
High level skills in facilities maintenance and construction, including carpentry, electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling systems, well systems, painting, fencing
Skills with welding, metal fabrication, etc.

Demonstrated ability to conduct physical labor outdoors in desert environment/wilderness setting (including excessive heat conditions), where wildlife encounters can be frequent (including rodents, snakes, spiders, bighorn sheep, coyotes, etc.). Ability to hike several miles over rugged terrain and lift minimum of 50 lbs.
Experience supervising employees or volunteers

Basic computer skills including use of Windows or Macintosh operating systems. Ability to operate email, word processing and use of spreadsheets software. Proven ability to organize, file, prioritize, manage time, write clearly, and interact well with supervisors, colleagues, and reserve users.
Proficiency operating tractors with backhoe and front end loader attachments
Able to anticipate and identify potential health and safety hazards; and willingness to confront and communicate effectively, and safely, to trespassers.

Basic understanding of state and federal agencies and regulatory policies that apply to research and land management issues, and general knowledge of conservation issues in relation to reserve management.
Able to become sufficiently familiar with BDC operating procedures in order to manage the reserve in the absence of directors and other administrative personnel.

Ability to learn and interpret to visitors the basic natural history of the reserve, including the names of plants, animals, geological formations. Become familiar with regional places, roads and history of the reserve and surrounding region.

Thorough knowledge in the areas of building space planning, codes, capacity, security, fire safety, organization and departmental principles and procedures involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences.
Thorough interpersonal skills including good service orientation and effective problem solving.
Thorough and effective skills to multi-task and prioritize daily activities effectively.
